headline: Single-cell models infer developmental dynamics and disentangle perturbation responses
label: Single Cell Dynamics Perturbation Modeling
summary: Preprints infer vector fields, Jacobians and coupled RNA–chromatin trajectories from time courses while disentangling perturbation effects from cell state.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit dynamical inference from single-cell snapshots. COATI applies unbalanced synchronized optimal transport to reconstruct coupled scRNA and scATAC trajectories across held-out stages. scJDO2 estimates per-cell score and flow Jacobians via entropic OT and states what local operators can and cannot identify. LADD fits a stochastic developmental vector field and finds observed lineage paths diverge from minimum-action routes. PhysInfer infers bursting kinetics from static data, and scSLIDE (Cell) orders samples along disease trajectories. A second line targets perturbation prediction with factorized latents. PertVI separates mitotic phase, state, batch and treatment, scDisentangle generates identity-preserving counterfactuals, scBIG++ predicts full-gene responses, and LingoCell adds language-guided in silico perturbation. scHiR integrates scRNA-seq with scHi-C. Simulators with known ground truth (scDeepSim, scCircaSim, PRISM for vertex-model inference) support controlled benchmarking. spSheaf, scCont and KQE-2 quantum clustering are adjacent.
